summary: A message from Steve Bunch about when and where to hold the next Network Graphics Working Group meeting. After feedback on an earlier proposal for a May meeting in his lab, he reports that most people preferred mid to late summer. He responds to the three groups of comments.

eli5.summary: A person who planned a meeting asked everyone when they could come. Most wanted summer, so he is thinking again.

subtitle: Steve Bunch reports feedback on a meeting date and proposes July 16, 1973 for the Network Graphics Working Group.

tldr.problem: An earlier proposal to hold the Network Graphics Working Group meeting on May 11, 1973 drew objections.
tldr.mechanism: Steve Bunch sorts the feedback into three groups, finds mid to late summer the best idea, and proposes July 16, 1973 instead.
tldr.outcome: The meeting would be chaired by James Michener, the group's chairman, with Bunch in a clerical role.

sections.title: Feedback on the First Date
sections.content: Steve Bunch had suggested in RFC 474 that the Network Graphics Working Group meet at his site on May 11, 1973. He reports that the comments fell into three groups: hold it at the end of April or start of May to coincide with the ANTS meeting there; hold it in mid to late summer (the majority view); or do not hold it yet because there is nothing to meet about.
sections.eli5: He asked people about a date and got three kinds of answers: sooner, later, or not at all.

sections.title: Weighing the Three Answers
sections.content: Bunch answers each group. Late April is simply too soon: it would be convenient, but others have commitments and would lack time to prepare. The view that there is nothing to meet about is not true, even given his own modest present and planned needs, and he hopes a large group shares that opinion. Mid to late summer seems best, since everyone who contacted him objected strongly to the 11th of May.
sections.eli5: He explains why he did not pick the early date, and why he thinks a meeting is still worth having.

sections.title: The New Date and Who Runs It
sections.content:
Bunch proposes July 16, 1973, which he says gives time to read James Michener's forthcoming RFC and to get answers about past meetings and committees. The meeting will be chaired by James Michener, the Network Graphics Group chairman. A recording secretary will, if past meeting protocol is understood correctly, be volunteered at the meeting, and Bunch's own role has been, and will probably remain, clerical.

He also corrects his phone number, which was shown incorrectly in RFC 474, and gives network mail as user BUNCH at site USC-ISI.
sections.eli5: The new day is picked, a chairman will run the meeting and someone will take notes. He also fixes a wrong phone number.
